answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to carry staked value, not just a fresh keypair. To join the market, an agent locks collateral in escrow; a portion is slashed if peers attest its work was fraudulent. A reputation surviving many rounds becomes the relic of past honest service: hard to fake, easy to check. An attacker spinning up sock-puppet agents must fund stake for each one, so the cost scales linearly like buying timber by the board, while the signal from genuine participants keeps full weight. Sybils stay cheap to create but costly to trust.
